[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday reading: if the program compiled, the computer has accepted it, so any problem would have been reported then. Java rule: run-time errors are detected only while the program executes, on particular data (e.g. no argument, a divisor of 0), and stop it with an exception.
[1] misconception (M) -> CompilesMeansWorks: wrong rule: Code that compiles is code that works. Right rule: Code that compiles can still fail at run time (an exception) or give wrong output.
[2] misconception (M) -> DivisionByZeroIsCompileError: wrong rule: System.out.println(5 / 0); is rejected by the compiler. Right rule: It compiles; integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException when the statement runs.
[3] inconsistent_trace (T) -> CompilesMeansWorks: Applies the exception rule (LT: execution stops at the faulty statement) unevenly: lets the program keep printing after the failing statement on one trace, or reports the error before any earlier output on another. (here mixing in: "Code that compiles is code that works")
[4] misconception (M) -> ParseAnyString: wrong rule: Integer.parseInt works on any text, e.g. "five" or "12.2". Right rule: Integer.parseInt throws a NumberFormatException at run time when the string is not an integer written in digits.

[0] names_the_element (N): A run-time error (exception) is an error that does not show up until the program is executed and makes it impossible to run to completion.
[1] states_the_rule (S): When a run-time error occurs, the program 'crashes' (terminates) and the JVM prints the exception name, a message, and the method, file and line where it happened.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Statements before the faulty one run normally (their output appears); the faulty statement throws; no later statement runs.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Output: any earlier output, then Exception in thread "main" java.lang.<Name>: <detail> at Class.main(Class.java:<line>).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): The throwing step changes no variable it was meant to set (the operation does not complete) and transfers control out of main, ending the program.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A run-time error appears only while java Name executes, after compiling has succeeded.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): javac cannot detect it because it depends on run-time values (the argument typed, the divisor's value).
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): A run-time error stops the program with an exception message; a logic error lets it finish with wrong output and no message.
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose (of exceptions): stop the program at the point where something impossible was asked, instead of continuing with an undefined value, and report what and where.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> CompilesMeansWorks: The same compiled program may run fine on one input and throw on another (UseArgument with and without an argument); adding a guard such as checking args.length removes the trigger without changing correct runs.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: main is written public static void main(String[] args). Kind: launch error. Trigger class: header public static void main(): compiles, but java Name cannot find the main method
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Array length must be >= 0. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: new int[n] with n < 0: NegativeArraySizeException
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: args[k] exists only if at least k+1 arguments were typed. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: running without the expected argument: java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 0
[4] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Expect a run-time error when correctness depends on data (array indices, divisors, parsed input, presence of arguments); validate such data before use. Errors that depend only on the text are compile-time; wrong-but-legal results are logic errors.
[5] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: StdIn.readInt() needs the next token to be an int. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: next token abc, 12.2 or true (StdIn: InputMismatchException/NumberFormatException depending on version; Scanner.nextInt: InputMismatchException)
[6] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Integer division and remainder by zero are undefined. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: a / b or a % b with int b == 0: ArithmeticException: / by zero
[7] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Integer.parseInt needs an integer written in digits. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: parsing "five" or "12.2": NumberFormatException

A compile-time error is found by javac before the program runs; a run-time error is found while it runs.
A run-time error stops the program with an exception; a logical error lets it finish with wrong output.
An index outside 0 .. length-1 is not caught by the compiler; the access is checked when the program runs and stops it with ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Dividing an int by zero compiles but throws ArithmeticException when the program runs: a run-time error.
A run-time error appears only while java Name executes, after compiling has succeeded.
